title: Name every button on the event page
prompt:
A screen reader lists Ticketly's buttons as "times, button, Book now, Book now, Book now, newsletter-cta". Fix the names without changing what sighted users see:

1. The `.close` "×" button needs a name containing "Close" (or "Dismiss"); the "×" itself shouldn't be read.
2. The icon-only `.search` button needs the name "Search".
3. Each `.book` button needs a unique name that **starts with "Book now"** and includes its pass (Friday, Saturday or Weekend).
4. The `.subscribe` button's name must contain its visible word "Subscribe".
hints: Hide the × with <span aria-hidden="true">, then add visually hidden text or an aria-label on the button.
Give each heading and each Book now button an id, then aria-labelledby="button-id heading-id" on the button.
For Subscribe, the simplest fix is deleting the aria-label so the button's content becomes its name.
explanation: The close button's name now comes from visually hidden text (or an aria-label), and the × is hidden so it isn't read as "times". The search button gets its name from aria-label because it has no text content, and its decorative SVG is hidden. Each Book now button uses aria-labelledby to reference itself and its card's heading, producing "Book now Friday pass": unique in a list of buttons, and still starting with the visible words, so voice control users can say "click Book now" (2.5.3 Label in Name). The Subscribe button was the easiest: removing a wrong aria-label let the visible text become the name again.

checks.close-named: The close button is named Close (or Dismiss) and the × isn't read
checks.search-named: The search button is named Search
checks.book-unique: The three Book now buttons have unique names that include their pass
checks.label-in-name: Every name contains its visible text, and Book now names start with it
